q: What is the shuttlecock’s top speed?
Calculate the ball’s acceleration in the first second.
9.7 / 1 = about 9.7 m/s², close to g = 9.8 m/s².
Explain why the shuttlecock stops speeding up.
As it speeds up, air resistance increases until it equals its weight: no resultant force, so it falls at terminal velocity.
The ball’s line becomes very slightly less steep. Explain why.
Air resistance on the ball also grows with speed, so the resultant force (weight − drag) gets a little smaller, and so does the acceleration.
